subject: Temporary cross-border processing window & subprocessor disclosure
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme-analytics.com>
To: alex_martinez
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2025-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data residency, subprocessors, and cross-region handling questions

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the product demo last week — the latency profile looked good. Before we move to a pilot, our security and legal teams have a few concrete asks around data residency and subprocessors:

- Can Redwood commit to keeping Acme customer data (including prompts and generated responses) within the EU for all production inference?
- If you do any cross-border processing (e.g., US-based hardware for failover or bursting), what is the maximum duration data may be processed outside the EU? Is there a guaranteed deletion window?
- Please provide the current list of subprocessors and their regions. We need to confirm none are in jurisdictions blocked by our policy.
- Do you support customer-managed KMS with keys seeded in EU regions?
- Any relevant artifacts (DPA, SOC 2 evidence, diagram of processing paths) would be helpful.

Our timeline: a 30-day pilot starting early Oct would be ideal if we can resolve these.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Turner
Director, Platform Security
Acme Analytics
From: alex_martinez
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, neha_kapoor, security@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2025-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency, subprocessors, and cross-region handling questions

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I want to be explicit and practical about what Redwood can commit to for Acme's pilot and what would require an enterprise Private engagement. High-level summary up front:

- EU Primary Residency: We can serve production inference from EU-only capacity and pin your model/data to EU-only tenants for the pilot.
- Controlled ephemeral cross-border processing: for latency or capacity burst scenarios, we can allow a controlled cross-border processing "ephemeral window" with the following constraints:
  * Duration: any request that is routed out of EU will be processed transiently and all request-derived state (KV caches, temporary logs) will be deleted within 24 hours of the request completion; the request record will remain in access logs for up to 90 days for troubleshooting and audit purposes.
  * Scope: ephemeral routing will apply only to inference execution (model compute) — we will not replicate persistent customer assets or training artifacts across regions.
  * Safeguards: data-in-transit TLS + AES-256 at-rest; we will apply EU-hosted KMS for keys whenever the request originates from a EU-pinned tenant.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current CSV export of our subprocessors and region mapping. We perform vendor risk assessments and can exclude specific subprocessors for enterprise Private installs.
- DPA & Evidence: attaching a draft DPA (redwood-dpa-draft-v2.pdf) and a processing-path diagram (processing-path-diagram.png) showing the ephemeral routing flow. SOC 2 reports are available under NDA — we can share with your security team if helpful.

If these constraints look reasonable, we can:
1) Enable an EU-pinned pilot cluster for Acme with EU KMS keys.
2) Enable ephemeral cross-border window limited to 24 hours and restricted to burst inference only; we can instrument monitoring to report exact volumes and percent of total requests.

Next steps: if you want, I can propose the exact wording we would add to the DPA for the 24-hour ephemeral processing carve-out and loop in legal.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz

Date: 2025-09-15T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency, subprocessors, and cross-region handling questions

Alex — quick internal note before we finalize:

1) The 24-hour deletion window for ephemeral caches is reasonable as a pilot commitment, but legal will want explicit language that: deletion includes KV cache shards, ephemeral logs, and any temporary models spawned for batching.
2) We should offer an optional configuration: EU-only KMS (customer-managed) vs Redwood-managed EU KMS; customers should be able to enforce customer-managed for regulated tenants.
3) For the DPA clause, recommend we add a monitoring and reporting commitment for the pilot: weekly volume and percent-of-requests that used cross-border burst routing.
4) Confirm that data retained in access logs (90 days) is pseudonymized (request ids only) and that mapping to customer identifiers requires a Redwood ops ticket.

I'll coordinate with Neha for the legal phrasing — Neha, can you draft two short DPA addenda: (A) pilot addendum covering ephemeral routing and deletion, plus (B) enterprise addendum for Dedicated/Private installs that removes ephemeral routing entirely?

Vanessa
Senior Sales Operations Manager
From: alex_martinez
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz, neha_kapoor, security@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2025-09-16T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency, subprocessors, and cross-region handling questions

Hi Sophie — following internal alignment (copied Vanessa and Neha), here's a consolidated response we can commit to for the Oct pilot and our recommended path forward:

Committed pilot items (EU-pinned):
- Production inference will be served from EU-pinned capacity.
- Ephemeral cross-border processing: enabled but strictly controlled to "burst inference" only and limited to a 24-hour deletion window for ephemeral compute artifacts (KV cache shards, transient model worker state, and temporary logs).
- Access logs: retained for 90 days; logs will surface only request ids and timestamps by default. Mapping to customer identifiers (email, project id) requires a formal Redwood ops request and is logged.
- KMS: we will provide EU KMS support. For pilot, we will offer Redwood-managed EU KMS; if you require, we can enable customer-managed KMS keys seeded in EU in our Dedicated/Private offering (this requires configuration and separate contract).
- Subprocessors: attached is the current list (subprocessors-list-20250914.csv). If Acme flags any disallowed subprocessors for pilot usage, we will evaluate and provide mitigation paths (e.g., alternative vendor or Private deployment).

Artifacts attached and links:
- redwood-dpa-draft-v2.pdf (DPA draft with pilot addendum language)
- processing-path-diagram.png (visual of routing and ephemeral eviction)
- subprocessors-list-20250914.csv
- Shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/processed-eu-dpa-ACME-2025 (access requires Redwood share)

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie/Acme security to review the attachments and confirm any subprocessors to flag.
2) Neha to send a short pilot DPA addendum (2-3 paragraphs) that we can sign for the 30-day pilot.
3) If acceptable, we will spin the EU-pinned pilot cluster and provide a weekly cross-border routing report during the pilot.

If you want a one-pager that translates the technical controls into legal-friendly DPA language, I can get that over by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Alex
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
